expression_of_concern.citation: Editorial Expression of Concern: WWOX gene restoration prevents lung cancer growth in vitro and in vivo. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 2017;114(16):E3365. Inder M. Verma, Editor-in-Chief.
expression_of_concern.acquired: PMC5402418 PDF via framework/scripts/pmc_pow_fetch.py (Europe PMC fullTextXML 404; efetch db=pmc returns front matter only with the publisher's no-XML notice). 1 page, 1728 characters of text plus one embedded replacement figure stream, all four read.
expression_of_concern.what_it_says: Four things, and they are narrow. (1) The concern is confined to ONE panel of ONE figure: 'the editors wish to note that Fig. 1B, beta-actin panel, appears to have duplicated bands'. (2) The original data cannot settle it: the authors state that 'because this issue was first raised more than 7 years after publication, the original data are not available to confirm whether an error was made in the figure construction'. (3) The authors' position is that 'any error in figure construction does not affect their scientific conclusions'. (4) The remedy offered is a REPLICATE, not the original: an image from an experiment 'completed in 2014', republished inside the notice as the new Fig. 1B with its legend.
expression_of_concern.what_it_does_NOT_say: It is not a retraction and does not withdraw the paper. It does not find misconduct, and does not say the duplication was intentional. It does not say the conclusions are wrong - it records the authors' assertion that they are not. It does not extend to any other figure, to Table 1, to the in vivo experiments or to the Ad-WWOX construct itself. It does not state that the editors verified the 2014 replicate: every confirmatory sentence about that image is quoted from the authors ('the authors state'). It does not say who raised the issue.
expression_of_concern.editorial_status_note: PubMed types it ExpressionOfConcernIn and Europe PMC types it expression-of-concern, while the PNAS page footer prints the running head 'CORRECTION'. Recorded because the two labels carry different weight and the deposit carries both.

entries.proposition: VISUAL ATTESTATION - Figure 1 supports the reagent as described. In panel A endogenous Wwox is detected only in lanes 4 (U2020) and 5 (MCF-7) and is absent from lanes 1-3 (H1299, H460, A549); in panel B Wwox appears only in lanes 1, 4 and 7, the three Ad-WWOX-infected lanes, and is absent from every Ad-GFP and every uninfected lane.
entries.snippet: [FIGURE SURFACE - ATTESTATION, NOT A QUOTE] Figure 1 read as pixels at 5x from the 421x196 embedded stream. Panel A: WWOX row blank at lanes 1-3, band at lanes 4 and 5; beta-actin present in all 5 lanes. Panel B: WWOX row bands at lanes 1, 4, 7 only; beta-actin row present across all 9 lanes.
entries.anchor: Figure 1, panels A and B, whole figure

entries.proposition: VISUAL ATTESTATION, MEASURED - the beta-actin loading row of Figure 1B, the row the 2017 Editorial Expression of Concern says 'appears to have duplicated bands', is unusually uniform: integrated density across the nine lanes spans only 174,576 to 184,780, a ratio of 1.06. The strongest pairwise normalised cross-correlation between lane crops is 0.930 (lanes 8-9). 🔴 THIS NEITHER CONFIRMS NOR REFUTES THE EDITORS' FINDING and is not offered as doing so: at 421x196 with JPEG compression the instrument cannot resolve band-level identity, and the measurement is recorded for what it is - a uniformity statistic with its limits stated.

skills_considered.reason: The reading route. Section by section, every figure as pixels, and the expression of concern read first as its own source.

Not needed as a skill, though a full cascade was in fact run by hand and is recorded: Europe PMC fullTextXML 404, efetch db=pmc metadata-only with the publisher's no-XML notice, PMC HTML behind reCAPTCHA, Europe PMC HTML JavaScript-rendered, Europe PMC render PDF HTTP 429, and finally the PMC PDF deposit through framework/scripts/pmc_pow_fetch.py, which succeeded at difficulty 4. The same route was run twice, once for the article and once for the expression of concern.

🔴 R4 THRESHOLD CHECK RUN MECHANICALLY. All 18 consolidated baseline claims enumerated from claim_registry_current.md and their titles read: every one is WWOX-DEE neurobiology, human genotype-phenotype, prenatal cortical development, network physiology, myelin or WW-domain biochemistry. The paper's therapeutic content is a 2005 adenoviral restoration in lung cancer lines; it yields no biomarker, no small molecule, no pathway correction and no repurposing candidate transferable to a WWOX-DEE genotype class. Its one durable contribution to this corpus is the reagent identity and the epistemic status of a paper under an expression of concern, and both belong in the dossier.
No molecule, no dose, no CNS endpoint, no target engagement in a neural system. T3 material cannot mature a therapeutic lever.

group_assessment.weighting: The Croce/Huebner laboratory at Ohio State, with Aqeilan as a mid-list author early in his career - the counts above are Huebner's (408 publications, 131 with FHIT, 32 with WWOX); Aqeilan RI stands at 137 and 65 today, but in 2005 he was a postdoctoral member of this group, not yet the head of the WWOX-DEE laboratory. This is the group that discovered WWOX and it is unambiguously primary FOR THE GENE. It is not primary for the disease: there is no patient, no germline variant, no neurological phenotype and no WWOX-DEE material anywhere in the study. Consequences applied throughout: first-hand weight to the adenoviral construct, the cell lines and the xenograft system, which are theirs; interpretation weight to every therapeutic sentence, which generalises from four immortalised lung cancer lines to 'WWOX gene therapy'; and a separate, explicit weighting for the fact that one figure of this paper carries a standing editorial expression of concern, which is recorded above and reflected in what the dossier says the paper may be cited for.

corpus_crossquery.query: Is the Ad-WWOX construct of this paper the reagent any other reading in this corpus depends on, and does anything here bear on a consolidated baseline claim about WWOX restoration or rescue?
corpus_crossquery.note: Three surfaces answered. (1) full_text_queue_current.md FT-076 already records this PMID as the source of the Ad-WWOX construct and as a multi-hop debt from PMID 20530675, this actor's wave-1 paper - so the reading closes a debt this actor itself opened. (2) claim_registry_current.md CLAIM 002 and CLAIM 004 are consolidated baseline claims about WWOX RESTORATION producing rescue - AAV-WWOX in organoids and AAV9-WWOX neuron-targeted in vivo. Both are a different vector, a different tissue, a different disease and a different endpoint, and neither cites this paper; this reading does NOT touch them, and the resemblance is thematic only. Saying so explicitly because 'restoring WWOX rescues' is exactly the sentence that would carry across contexts unexamined. (3) paper_registry_current.md holds no record for PMID 16223882, so a new paper record is proposed rather than an existing one amended.
